_comment: Same values as tokens.css, for SVG assets, MapLibre styles and Android. Edit both together.

color._w186_scul: W186 palette (SPEC §328): his 'SCUL keeps its own paints'. pulsar is the app chrome's, as before her palette (the Log's header, a nova, the pills, the flash, the ships' bell; the map's is color-map's, her yellow; Plain's chrome reads her yellow's words, tokens.css). scul-luna, scul-course and scul-black-hole: SCUL's ships (app/ship-model.js PAINT), its boot ring (app/hexload.css) and the funk, the pink, orange and violet they were (luna is her paid places' orange now, course the route's accent, black-hole grey). rider-cheeks: Plain's rider's blush (RIDER_PAINT), its own name, as orange means paid places.
color._w186_avatars: W186 palette (SPEC §328): the avatar swatches (app/avatar.js COLORS), the marker's own paint in both themes: her accent, yellow, red, green and silver by night. Were W157 avatars5's hivis and gold beside negi, luna, you and black-hole.

color-light._comment: Daystar, the light theme for riding by day: the same concepts and keys as color, each hue darkened to read on a pale ground (WCAG AA for text, 3:1 for lines and icons; chart/style/test_build_style.py checks them). The dark values above stay the default.
color-light._w138_dayink: W138 dayink (her note, 2026-10-24: 'the same bright blue for bike Lanes in light mode instead of ... the teal'): wormhole, the bike paths' names and the chrome's bike blue, is the bike lines' azure (bike-line, hue 203) at the old teal's lightness, 6.2:1 on the ground and 5.6:1 on the cards. Was #006478.
color-light._w86_map: W86 map (the feedback form, 2026-10-22: 'The whole map is too purple, especially in light mode. That reduces the contrast on a sunny day'): the chart's ground, buildings, hairlines, secondary ink and streets are the W68 chrome's cool slate and graphite, and the water a pale blue-grey with a muted indigo rim (apart from the bike paths' teal), where they were lavender and indigo. Purple stays for the accents: the black holes, the town glow (its sprite keeps the old nebula purples: chart/style/build_style.py DAY_SPRITE_ACCENTS), the kind words. Was void #f6f3fc, space-1 #ebe6f7, space-3 #d3caee, stardust #4e4777, starpath #3d28a8, nebula #cfc6f7, nebula-glow #5640e0.
color-light._w186_course: W186 palette (SPEC §328), his ruling: course is the route's chrome (pins, time bubbles, the turn card and arrows, distances, the arrival time), her accent, no longer the orange; course-line the route's line before its stretches are rated, the other options (at 40 %) and the lead to the start, her grey. The rated line is the quality scale's.
color-light._w171_palette: W171 palette (SPEC §299, her row of 2026-10-26 18:33): harbour, the app's accent in Plain where SCUL keeps phosphor (titles, selected text and icons, links, the Log's chart, the loading bar), and harbour-fill, the selected fill. tokens.css applies them to Plain in one rule. Light's harbour is also the launch screen's ground (app/build.mjs).
color-light._w192_avatar: W192 icons7 (SPEC §338), her row of 2026-10-29 06:04: 'In light mode, purple avatars should take on the darker purple accent color of light mode. All other avatar colors can stay the same across dark and light mode.' The purple avatar on a light map (the marker, the pictures and the swatch: app/avatar.js paintOf), her day accent; the other four have no twin.

color-light-chrome._comment: W68 daylook: Daystar's chrome (the bar, the sheets, Settings, the Log, the search) in a cool slate and graphite, where it was the chart's lavender and indigo: arclight, 2026-10-20, 'green on purple, which is just a very weird color scheme'. The chart keeps color-light. These override color-light's in the app's CSS only (tokens.css); the phosphor is a little deeper, for 4.5:1 on the cards. chart/style/test_build_style.py checks them.

color-amoled._comment: AMOLED black, in Dark only: the void and the chrome's surfaces become pure black, which an OLED pixel draws by switching off. Every other colour is the dark one.

palette._comment: W186 palette (SPEC §328): her 'Starchart colours' (her row of 2026-10-28 10:10, his 'Yes, do it'), by name, one hue for each, a night and a day value. <name> is the fill (icons, map lines, bars and blocks), <name>-words the words (text and thin lines); where her day words are 'ink', the day ink's value. ink, accent, silver and shading are hers; ground her map's night ground; card, sheet and hairline her night surfaces. The roles read these (color, color-light, color-map, quality, mbta, the Plain rule in tokens.css); app/tests/colours.test.mjs holds her table and the contrast of every pair she set.
palette._veto: W186 palette: the pairs she set that fall short, each the nearest shade that passes (veto points, SPEC §328). night grey-icon: the grey icons' fill under their drawing (her ink on her grey gives 2.45:1; the drawing is white, the sign's, and her grey 4 % toward black gives it 3:1). day orange-icon: the paid squares' fill under the white drawing (her day orange gives 2.59:1; 3:1 at 8 % toward black). night magenta-words: the Commuter Rail's name on the ground (4.48:1; 4.5:1 at 1 % toward white). A hazard's 'ink drawing' on her yellow is the day ink in both themes (her night ink on yellow is 1.17:1). day orange-line: construction's dashed line on the day ground (her day orange gives 2.35:1; 3:1 at 12 % toward black). night grey-words: the grey words on her shading, Plain's chosen route card's note and the Log's selected flight's line (her grey gives 4.48:1; 4.5:1 at 1 % toward white; by day hers give 4.59:1).

color-map._comment: W186 palette (SPEC §328): the chart's colours by night where they differ from the app chrome's (color), under the same role names: the map's are shared by both word modes, and SCUL's chrome keeps color. chart/style/build_style.py and design/glyphs/build.py read color overlaid with these. void the ground, space-1 the buildings' fill (her cards), space-2 her sheets, space-3 the buildings' edge (her hairlines), stardust the grid lines and district names (grey), starlight the map's ink, negi red, caution and pulsar (the traffic lights) yellow.
color-map._w186_icons: W186 palette: the place icons. drawing: the paid and free places' drawing, black by night and white by day (her 'drawing white by day, black #000000 at night'); free: the free places' blue square, her blue; grey-icon: the grey places' fill (racks, bike and car parking, bike share, police, bus stops) under a white drawing, the veto shade. icon-edge: her thin ink outline round the orange, yellow and cyan icons by day; by night the ground's, one step off it so the Daystar sheet's swap can tell them apart.

color-map-light._comment: W186 palette: the chart's by day, over color-light: the map's ink, red, yellow, the bike paths' names (her cyan words) and the icons' drawing, free blue and grey.

glass._comment: Wave 21: the chrome's see-through fills and its hairline's colour, as #rrggbbaa. btn: buttons, the top row and the bar; card: the readout, banners, turn card and sheets over the chart; edge: the 1 px hairline. Same values as tokens.css --glass-btn, --glass-card and --glass-edge. Never blurred (brief 8).

color-fixed._comment: W185 colours (SPEC §321): the named colours that are the same in both themes and both modes, by role. Apart from color, so the Daystar swaps (chart/style/build_style.py day_table, design/glyphs/build.py TOKEN_OF) leave them as they are. tokens.css has the ones the CSS reads, as --fixed-<name>.
color-fixed._roles: white and black: the ends of a mix (lighter, darker). drawing: the places' one white drawing. highlight: a glyph's white highlight, top left of its rim. sign: a road sign's white (the stop sign's rim, the roundel's disc, a pin's star, the turn arrow). t-ink: the roundel's T. housing: a traffic signal's black housing. cone-band: a cone's reflective band. favourite: the favourites' star. shadow: every shadow's black. shade-day: Daystar's shadow, a slate at half alpha (app/theme.css --shade). paper: a sticker's die-cut edge. qr-light and qr-dark: a QR code's modules, black on white to scan.

mbta._comment: W185 colours: the MBTA's line colours by night, red the Red Line and Mattapan, purple the Commuter Rail; W186 palette: her night fills (red, orange, blue, green, and magenta for the Commuter Rail), where they were the MBTA brand's. The style lifts or deepens them on each ground (build_style.py TRACK_BOLD); mbta-track has the results the app's CSS draws.
mbta._w192_buses: W192 icons7 (SPEC §338), her row of 2026-10-29 05:59: 'The bullet points for bus times should be in yellow. Silver line bus times can stay gray, while blue line shuttle times should be blue.' A bus's colour by the feed's own route_color (app/comets-logic.js lineColour): bus the local buses (the MBTA's bus yellow FFC72C), her yellow; silver the Silver Line (7C878E), her grey; shuttle the airport shuttles (Massport's 0e3475), her blue. Were all her grey (W186 palette).

mbta-day._comment: W186 palette (SPEC §328): Daystar's line colours, her day fills (the Orange Line's track her #cd7617); the stations' rings take these in both themes.
mbta-day._w192_buses: W192 icons7: by day her day fills; the yellow takes her thin ink edge on a card (app/comets.css .cdot.pale).

mbta-track._comment: W185 colours: the Layers tile's tracks (app/layers.css), the style's TRACK_BOLD by theme: Dark's Orange Line in a tunnel, and Daystar's Orange Line deepened, on the ground and in a tunnel. chart/style/test_build_style.py holds them to the style's.

quality._comment: W185 colours: the ride-quality scale (W173 quality3, SPEC §301), the same in both themes: good the bike lanes and paths (Dark's wormhole cyan), then the continuum from the quietest streets (green) through yellow and orange to the worst (red); edge Daystar's thin ink edge under them, the chart's starlight by day. app/comfort-along.js QUALITY_INK, the Layers tile, the legend's ramp.

map._comment: W185 colours: the chart's own colours that no app chrome shares, by theme (chart/style/build_style.py). dark: lamp the lit streets' warm white (W112 palette), street-name (W160 mapclean), medical the medical stops' names, nebula-name and black-hole-name. light: street-name (W150 mapink), park and water the fills (W88 mapfix), bike the bike icons' and words' azure (W160 mapclean; W186 palette: her cyan words, #0b6da1); the Daystar sprite's two purple accents (W86 map) went in W186 palette. W186 palette, hers: dark nebula-name the water's names (was a violet), black-hole-name the roundabouts' grey (was a violet), parking the lots' fill; light water-name, her shores' and names' slate (the style draws color-light's nebula-glow, the same), parking.

motion._w69_comment: W69 motion: the motion language (design/ART.md, Motion; SPEC §107), the same as tokens.css

shape._comment: W69 artdir (design/ART.md): the corners in px, as tokens.css --r-*; by role: inner a tile inside a card, card anything floating over the chart, sheet the top corners of a bottom sheet, pill every control

space._comment: W69 artdir: the spacing scale in px, as tokens.css --sp-1 … --sp-6

glyph._comment: Map glyph construction (64-unit viewBox), from the brand lane
